in_text_mentions: of her presenting symptoms. A computerized tomography (CT) scan of the brain showed no signs of acute intracranial hemorrhage or infarction and was notable for advanced temporal lobe dominant cerebral atrophy, which correlated with her dementia. Incidentally, the CT revealed a possible right open lip schizencephaly with hypoplastic corpus callosum as depicted in Figure 1A–C which show evaluation by CT and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain, confirming the presence of a cleft extending from the right cerebral cortex into the lateral ventricle, consistent with open lip schizencephaly.
